agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-01 step 4 of 5
summary_for_principal: Step 4 of 5, and the milestone this whole work package has been building toward: the spec's own full worked example (Appendix A, 'grounded inquiry') now loads, resolves and validates end-to-end with zero problems reported, through the actual command-line tool a person or another program would run. Built the two checkers the spec names, a `validate`/`explain` command line tool, and a complete supporting cast (every Tool, Profile and Control Appendix A calls) so there was something real to validate against — then proved that removing any single one of them makes validation correctly refuse it. Building this surfaced one real gap: a value's own 'this is a profile-shaped thing' declaration was never actually checked against the real profile it named, anywhere in the format — now fixed. 55 new tests, all passing on every supported Python version.

decisions.headline: Type strings (`profile:<id>@<version>`, bare or nested in `list<...>`/`map<...>`) are now checked for resolution (V2) wherever they're declared — Tool inputs/outputs, Process inputs/host_inputs/state.
decisions.problem: Building the Appendix A corpus for A2 found that removing a referenced Profile (e.g. `brief@1`) produced no V2 finding at all: nothing anywhere checked that a declared type's embedded profile reference actually resolves, only that structural references (a Tool's own `controls[]`, a Step's `tool:`) did.
options_rejected: Leave it unchecked, since it's not explicitly named as its own line in spec §14's V-rule table: rejected — a `profile:<ref>` in a type string is exactly the same kind of reference V2 already governs (spec §1.2, 'a reference to another definition is id@version'), just appearing inside a type string instead of a dedicated field; refusing to check it would mean a broken profile reference in the single most common place profiles appear (typed inputs/outputs/state) silently passes.
decisions.cost_to_change: One regex-based walker (_v2_profile_type_refs) called from validate_tool and validate_process; no fixture depends on the old, narrower behaviour.

evidence.claim: Removing tests/definition/fixtures/appendix_a_corpus/brief.profile.yaml from the registry produced zero findings before this fix, despite the Process's own inputs.brief being declared profile:brief@1.
evidence.source: measured directly while building tests/definition/test_appendix_a.py, before the fix

decisions.revisit_if: Never expected — this closes a real hole in V2's own stated coverage.

decisions.headline: The pass+fail example requirement (spec §5.2) now applies to any Tool that returns `profile:control-result@1`, not only ones declaring `checker_for`.
decisions.problem: decision-evidence@1 is a checker by spec's own definition (returns control-result@1) but is wired through decision@1's `checker:` field rather than a generic `checker_for` role, since it checks one specific profile rather than every control of a kind. The V3 check written in step 3 only looked at `checker_for`, so decision-evidence@1 would have escaped the requirement entirely.
options_rejected: Give decision-evidence@1 a `checker_for` anyway, just to satisfy the existing check: rejected — `checker_for: { control: PROFILE }` already names profile-conformance@1's specific generic role (spec §5.2's own example); reusing it for a specialised checker would misdescribe what decision-evidence@1 actually is.
decisions.cost_to_change: One helper function (_is_checker) and a one-line change to what v3_checker_examples gates on.

evidence.claim: spec §5.2: 'A checker is a CODE Tool that declares what it checks and returns profile:control-result@1' — the defining property is what it returns, not the checker_for field, which spec's own example uses only for the generic profile-conformance case.

measured.method: Ran the full suite on the container's default 3.11; isolated venvs for 3.10 and 3.12 running tests/definition directly.
measured.result: 200/200 passing on 3.11 (full suite); 171/171 passing on 3.10 and 3.12 (tests/definition).

lessons.maxim: A 'closed set of fixtures references everything, and removing any one breaks something' acceptance criterion (WP-01 A2) is itself a strong forcing function for finding gaps in a reference-checking rule — build the full fixture set and prove the negative (removal breaks it) before declaring the rule complete, rather than trusting the rule's own unit tests alone.
lessons.incident: Rule V2's own unit tests (step 2) all passed, yet Appendix A's corpus revealed a whole class of reference — a type string's embedded profile:<ref> — that V2 never checked at all, only surfaced by literally removing a real fixture and watching nothing complain.
lessons.destination: any future WP-01-style validator work, and any future PR that adds a new place a reference can appear in this format
